priority-tax-relief.title: Priority Tax Relief
priority-tax-relief.heroSentence: First design hire at a 200-person, $7M MRR tax relief firm. Rebuilt the brand, established product and design strategy, released foundation design system for print and screens, solo.

dossier.role: Brand & Product Designer — first dedicated design hire
dossier.team: Solo — embedded with engineering, marketing, and senior leadership
dossier.stakes: $7M MRR national tax relief firm, no prior design function
dossier.status: Shipped — live brand system, component library, replatformed site

priority-tax-relief.body: There was no design system, no component library, and no evidence-based process — decisions were made on opinion. I analyzed the full paying-customer database in Jupyter and ran cross-department stakeholder interviews to ground brand and product decisions in real data. Then built the infrastructure the company had never had: a brand system, a component library engineering could use without a designer in the room, and a redesigned customer funnel that increased conversion opportunities 14×. I also led the marketing site's replatform from WordPress to Django/Wagtail — Lighthouse performance went from 68 to 91–100, accessibility from 64 open issues to AA WCAG compliant.

heroArtifact.alt: Priority Tax Relief brand guideline pages — logo lockups, color system, usage rules

processArtifact.alt: Departmental process-mapping board from cross-department stakeholder research

seattle-creative-directory.title: Seattle Creative Directory
seattle-creative-directory.heroSentence: A self-initiated, full-stack platform mapping the Pacific Northwest creative tech ecosystem — still running, six years in, because nobody asked me to build it.

dossier.team: Solo — product, design, engineering, and research

seattle-creative-directory.body: No platform existed connecting Seattle's creative and technology community, so I built one — designed, developed, and still manage a full-stack directory using Next.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Vercel, with an information architecture supporting hundreds of creative businesses across location, discipline, and organization type. I run ongoing qualitative research into the community through interviews and podcast production (50K+ plays), and own the product vision, technical architecture, and long-term platform direction myself.

heroArtifact.alt: Seattle Creative Directory homepage — podcast guest quote grid

processArtifact.alt: Seattle Creative Directory filter taxonomy — size, neighborhood, and discipline facets

android-gemini.title: Android Gemini Studies
android-gemini.heroSentence: Before Android had a native model for AI, I spent six weeks working out what it should feel like in your hand — gesture first, not a chat box.

dossier.team: Dedicated interaction designer within a BUCK concept team (creative director, two motion designers, rotating designers)
dossier.stakes: Early Gemini: capability with no native UX paradigm on Android
dossier.status: Internal concept exploration for Google's Gemini team

android-gemini.body: In late 2023 Google had early Gemini capabilities but no interface model for a phone — AI meant a chat box, which is wrong for a device that is physical, gestural, and contextual. I took a loose body of early thinking and pressure-tested it into seven interaction-pattern families across four scenario clusters: drive-to-output flows, camera-as-AI-interface, contextual web actions, and AI personality tuning. The through-line was Dots & Handles — AI shouldn't just generate output, it should give you something to grab onto afterward.

heroArtifact.alt: Whats That style-spectrum slider concept frame

processArtifact.alt: Interaction-pattern storyboard exploring three variants of an AI action menu

resonance-ai.title: Resonance AI
resonance-ai.heroSentence: The sole product designer building trust into an AI product — where people had to act on machine-generated insight they couldn't independently verify.

dossier.team: Solo design, cross-functional with engineering/data science
dossier.stakes: Users acting on machine-generated insights with no way to verify them
dossier.status: Shipped to all active clients — drove an acquihire outcome

resonance-ai.body: No design system or visual language existed for the product's AI output, so I built one from scratch: type, iconography, chart language, and color system to support a growing product, plus the workflows that helped people interpret, validate, and act on machine-generated insight rather than just stare at it skeptically. Automated report compilation reduced analyst task time by 95% and moved reporting cadence from weekly to daily. The product's value drove an acquihire outcome for the company.

processArtifact.alt: Early chart-language and color-system exploration for the AI output

pwc.title: PwC Concourse
pwc.heroSentence: Built the mobile foundation an enterprise platform never had — adopted as the baseline across PwC's internal product ecosystem.

dossier.team: Sole designer on the responsive build, within a 12-person design team
dossier.stakes: Enterprise collaboration platform, US and British offices
dossier.status: Shipped — adopted as mobile baseline platform-wide

pwc.body: No mobile strategy existed for this enterprise collaboration platform — it was desktop-only. I researched how distributed teams across US and British offices actually managed complex projects and communication, then translated that organizational complexity into interaction models, reusable patterns, and a responsive mobile adaptation. The touch-adapted components I built were adopted as the baseline for all mobile work across PwC's internal product ecosystem — not just this product.

heroArtifact.alt: PwC Concourse responsive dashboard, anonymized per existing NDA guidance

lumedic.title: Lumedic
lumedic.heroSentence: In spring 2020, tens of thousands of hospital employees needed to prove their COVID status to get into work, and no trustworthy patient-controlled system existed. I designed it.

dossier.role: Product Designer — primary designer on the patient wallet
dossier.company: Lumedic, a Providence St. Joseph Health portfolio company
dossier.team: Primary designer on this platform within a 5-person design team
dossier.stakes: Trust handshake between patients, hospital verifiers, and issuers
dossier.status: Shipped on iOS, Android, and web — used across the Providence network

lumedic.body: Medical records live behind institutional firewalls; patients aren't parties to their own records. Lumedic inverted that: the patient holds their own verified credentials and shares them selectively. I owned the design across three releases — a UX audit of an Evernym boilerplate wallet, a multimodal architecture (phone-to-phone, phone-to-kiosk), and a Carbon Design System adaptation for native mobile — plus the issuer dashboard clinics used to bulk-upload vaccine records. Research with hospital employees showed people didn't need to understand the credential system, only the outcome. We dropped "blockchain" and most explanatory copy, and trust went up.

heroArtifact.alt: Lumedic verification kiosk — verified COVID-19 status state

processArtifact.alt: Lumedic holder-side flow — add connection, vaccination card, test result detail

providence.title: Providence Telestroke & Express Care
providence.heroSentence: Designed real-time clinical workflows where a slow or wrong interface had patient-safety consequences — not a hypothetical stakes claim, a literal one.

dossier.stakes: Real-time clinical workflow — patient outcomes during stroke response
dossier.status: Shipped — design system adopted by subsequent teams

providence.body: No clinician-tested information architecture existed for this telestroke workflow — field research with clinicians revealed the assumptions baked into the existing design were wrong, and inverted the information hierarchy entirely. I integrated the Epic API to bring live patient records into the workflow, adapted Material Design for a healthcare context with warmer, empathy-driven decisions, and worked directly in Storybook with engineering to eliminate handoff gaps. The resulting design system was adopted by subsequent teams in the Digital Innovation Group — it outlasted my time on the project.

heroArtifact.alt: Express Care Virtual information-architecture and workflow diagram

processArtifact.alt: Hand-annotated field research notes on the inverted telestroke hierarchy
